paper.title: GUIrilla: A Scalable Framework for Automated Desktop UI Exploration
paper.central_claim: 提出 GUIrilla：基于 macOS Accessibility API 的自动化桌面 UI 探索/爬取框架（含 handlers 与 GPT-4 辅助 agent），产出层级 MacApp Trees 与 GUIrilla-Task（27,171 任务/1,108 应用/4.2K 屏）；在其上微调的 GUIrilla-See(0.7B/3B/7B) 以仅 4.2K 屏幕在 ScreenSpot-v2/Pro 上达到有竞争力的 macOS 精度（7B：94.73/35.36）。作者强调这是数据爬取框架，不是自主 agent。

evidence.quote: GUIrilla remains a data crawler whose output is intended to train and stabilize downstream models

- • GUIrilla-Task dataset. A macOS, full-desktop corpus of 27,171 tasks across 1,108 applications and  4.2K unique screens. We also release GUIrilla-Gold (1,283 human-verified tasks) with a 90.26% human baseline.

Within the crawler’s core (highlighted in blue), multiple handlers address the common parsing challenges: Pop-up handler manages transient modal content, Invisible elements handler filters off-screen components present in accessibility, Unrolling menu items handler processes dynamically generated navigation elements, and Empty elements handler resolves placeholder elements with missing metadata. This multi-handler approach enables robust extraction of actionable interface information despite the underlying data quality issues.
1. The Input Agent : This agent generates contextually appropriate input strings based on the accessibility tree, ensuring relevant text is entered into form fields and search boxes.

2. The Order and Login Agent : Given a hierarchical list of on-screen elements, the agent determines an safest interaction sequence starting with elements that cause minimal UI changes and progressing to those with potentially significant effects (e.g., "Delete" buttons). Login pages are treated as a special case, requiring human input. This agent enhances the security and safety of the exploration process by avoiding random or destructive actions.

3. The Task Agents : After the uninstallation phase, these agents refine the resulting output tree, cleaning up duplicates, and transforming the structured data into a readable list of natural language tasks. Their inclusion enables both refinement and generation of more complex and natural language task descriptions.

While our framework leverages GPT-based agents to enable robust and secure interaction, both the application trees and task data can also be collected deterministically without GPT-4 requests by following a fixed element processing order and using default input string values. However, incorporating GPT-based reasoning significantly improves the safety and contextual relevance of interactions. A detailed comparison between deterministic and GPT-guided exploration is provided in Appendix A.8.2 .

- • Actions : A list of actions that can be executed without causing significant changes to the UI. We define a significant change as the addition or removal of more than 10 UI elements following an interaction.

As an application of the collected MacApp Trees, we derive a task-oriented dataset, GUIrilla-Task , by extracting function-centric interactions from tree edges. We deployed the GUIrilla crawler on 12,298 macOS applications using an open Mac App Store dataset ( Sergii Kryvoblotskyi, 2025 ) . Out of these, 1,108 applications supported the macOS Accessibility framework and yielded valid interaction trees.

We report task success rates based on action accuracy. For click tasks, success requires the predicted coordinates to fall within the target element’s bounding box. Input tasks additionally require exact text matches.

Accessibility metadata often reduces to generic labels like "button" or "text" without capturing functional intent. In contrast, GPT-generated descriptions understand visual context and explicit purpose. When UI screens contain similar elements, accessibility labels create ambiguous supervision signals that hinder target identification. Florence-0.7B achieved 53.55% accuracy on GPT-generated tasks versus 40.35% on accessibility-based tasks—a 13-point gap demonstrating that functional supervision outperforms surface-level properties for training UI agents.
- • Local-Only Operation : All collection, replay, and annotation occur entirely locally without requiring data transmission to third parties

The collected tasks were split into train and test subsets, such that the applications in test did not appear in train, and test applications contained larger, more complicated accessibility trees. There are 881 881 applications with 25,606 25,606 entries in train and 227 227 applications with 1,565 1,565 task entries in test.
- • Epochs: 4; total wall-clock time ≈ \approx 10 hours.

OneNote appears in train data (macOS app) and in ScreenSpot-v2 (Windows). This app has 1 task in the benchmark, and the login screen looks identical, so the leakage may have affected the result. We adjusted the score to account for it from 90.41% -> 90.33%. This doesn’t influence the ranking, yet we adjusted the score for fairness.
GUIrilla-See (7B) | macOS | Synthetic | 4.2K | 94.73% | 35.36% | 41.39%

Task Quality . From the 1319 original English language-based tasks, 84.3% of tasks were marked as DOABLE after manual verification. Comparing GPT strings to human edits, 91% required no change. The 109 edited cases showed 97% similarity to originals (Ratcliff/Obershelp), confirming minor edits. We release manully edited dataset as GUIrilla-Gold 7 7 7 https://huggingface.co/datasets/GUIrilla/GUIrilla-Gold/ .

Accessibility metadata quality varies significantly: 64% of screens received GOOD ratings, 24% MEDIUM, and 12% BAD. At the element level, only 40% have correct role and description pairs, while 49% contain role information only, and 11% are mislabeled. Bounding boxes are accurate for 80% of elements, though 10% extend outside the visible window.
- • Multi-step Tasks: Mark as NOT DOABLE if requiring multiple distinct actions

To assess performance variability, we re-evaluated all models using stochastic decoding with parameters: num_beams=3 , do_sample=True , temperature=0.3 . For each model, we conducted three independent runs and computed mean ± standard deviation of success rates.

Due to the differences in A11y tree APIs and tools supported by each operating system, we utilize pyatspi to access the A11y tree on Ubuntu, pywinauto on Windows, and ApplicationServices on macOS. We then simulate human-computer interactions by sampling actions from the obtained A11y tree. In our simulation environment, we employ two different exploration methods: Depth-First Search (DFS) and Random Walk.
GUIRILLA is not an autonomous agent; instead, it systematically collects realistic interaction traces and accessibility metadata

preliminary_evidence_judgment: Read before seat scores. GUIrilla crawls 12,298 macOS apps through the Accessibility API (handlers for pop-ups, invisible/empty elements, menus; optional GPT-4 input/order/login/task agents), yielding MacApp Trees for 1,108 apps and 27,171 single-step click/type tasks on about 4.2K screens; app-disjoint split (881/227 apps). Trained grounders (Florence-0.7B, Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B) improve on the in-house app-disjoint test and on ScreenSpot-v2/Pro (7B: 87.5->94.73, 27.13->35.36). Problems: A.3 'Prompts' section is empty; Gold count stated as 1,283 vs 1,319 audited vs 1,565 test tasks; leakage adjustment 90.41->90.33 matches no Table 6 value; 'agentic' Table 8 is single-step accuracy; handler ablation on 3 apps; no data-scaling curve or equal-size alternative corpus. The paper calls itself a data crawler whose output trains downstream models, so component_training applies. Applicable: gui K14/K23/C01; E05, E06, E26, E27, E28.
agreed_items_review: Agreed items G=2, X=2, E.measurement=2, E.causality=2, E.holdout=3, E.statistics=2, E.cost=2, evidence_level offline, claim_support scoped were re-checked; the three known reporting inconsistencies (A.3, Gold counts, leakage figure) are confirmed and already deducted.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported: LoRA fine-tuning on about 4.2K macOS screens / 25.6K crawler-derived tasks raises Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B grounding on an app-disjoint macOS test and on ScreenSpot-v2/Pro by roughly 7-8 points (7B: 94.73 / 35.36), and functional task descriptions train better than raw AX labels (Florence 53.55 vs 40.35); the crawler can run without GPT.
not_supported: Desktop agent / online task success ('agentic' Table 8 is single-step accuracy)
Data-efficiency superiority over OS-Atlas under matched conditions (A.7 has no table)

G.reason: macOS data scarcity and non-scalable manual annotation are real, but OS-Atlas already automates AX-based macOS collection and the 'crawler not released' contrast is disputed; the residual (handlers, functional labels, full-desktop trees) is only partly measured.

M.reason: Handlers and functional relabelling respond directly to observed AX failures and give distinguishable, tested predictions (handler vs random crawler; functional vs AX-label supervision 53.55 vs 40.35). Weak points: 80%-accurate boxes as training targets and single-step tasks framed toward desktop automation.

X.reason: Crawler modules, parameters, tree schema, split and training settings are described; the GPT-agent prompts are absent (A.3 empty), the random-crawler baseline is undefined, retry/stop rules and collection cost are missing, and Gold counts are inconsistent.

E.measurement.reason: External ScreenSpot-v2/Pro use human labels and clear point-in-box judging; the in-house test uses AX boxes (80% accurate) and GPT task strings, Table 8 'Success Rate' is single-step accuracy, and the leakage-adjusted figure does not reconcile with Table 6.

E.causality.reason: Clean base-vs-tuned controls on the same backbones and two small ablations; data-efficiency claims vs OS-Atlas/UGround mix backbone, data and recipe, and A.7's same-backbone claim has no table.

E.holdout.reason: App-disjoint 881/227 split with harder test apps, external ScreenSpot benchmarks and a manual overlap audit (OneNote/Excel disclosed); the adjusted score does not reconcile and everything is offline.

E.statistics.reason: Denominators given; three stochastic-decoding runs with SD (inference noise, not training seeds); handler ablation on 3 apps single-run; Gold denominators inconsistent.

E.cost.reason: Collection hardware, parallelism, training hours and GPUs are reported; GPT-4 API cost, total crawl time and any cost comparison with manual annotation or OS-Atlas are missing.
